inputs.original_text: Five months after the ceasefire was announced, families in Gaza are still living with airstrikes, gunfire and shelling. Ahmed Baroud, a displaced father of five in Deir al-Balah, says drones still buzz overhead and naval fire puts fishermen at risk. That is not real peace. Families need safety, stability and the ability to earn a living—not another promise on paper. Any lasting settlement has to restore order and make rebuilding possible; civilians should not be left to bear the cost of slogans and failed assurances.
inputs.modified_text: Five months after the ceasefire was announced, families in Gaza are still facing airstrikes, gunfire and shelling. That is what happens when promises are treated as a substitute for order and security. Ahmed Baroud, a displaced father of five in Deir al-Balah, says drones buzz overhead and naval fire puts fishermen at risk—people cannot rebuild their lives or earn a living under those conditions. The priority must be protecting civilians, restoring stability and making reconstruction possible, not repeating slogans while families pay the price.
